title: relay-run end absorbs a step whose parent is in a damaged local file without failing
lead: When `relay-run end` absorbs local events and a step's parent was in a local file it skipped as damaged, the step is still absorbed and the run still ends, with the orphan named on stderr.
findings_note: s332 relay 2026-10-16, later note 3: an absorbed step whose parent sits in a skipped damaged local file fails in the shared ledger
boundary: **Not in this slice:** repairing a damaged local file.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: s332's absorb-on-end (`ops._absorb`) skips a local file that cannot be read and reports it as unreadable. A step from another readable local file whose `--parent` was recorded in the skipped one is still copied into the shared ledger, where its parent does not exist; the s332 orchestrator found the shared ledger then fails to fold that run, and recovering needs a hand edit of the ledger.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ops.py`, `_absorb`; `src/slicer/relayrun.py` (`local_run_events`, `fold`).
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: the stderr line naming the orphaned step.
- `CHANGELOG.md` under Fixed. `tests/test_relay_run.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body: - `test_RelayRunEnd_ParentInDamagedLocalFile_EndsAndNamesOrphan`: two sibling local files, the parent's damaged; `end` exits 0, `relay-run list` shows the run, and stderr names the orphaned step.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Reproduce with the test and watch it go red.
2. Either hold back an orphaned step from the absorb or fold it without its parent; mutation-check.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
